stages.name: Correctness of the PostgreSQL write and read paths
Ship the image and prove the data

legs.goal: feature/non-prod-wave2-cutover contains every develop commit, with both sides' admin_db_service.py changes intact.
boundaries: a trial merge already showed this is a clean auto-merge; if a conflict appears, stop and report rather than resolving creatively
do not push to develop

legs.goal: The reconciled branch carries both the wave-2 work and the security branch, with all five write methods and the whole security suite intact.
boundaries: three files overlap; the security side's edits are small, wave 2's are large - preserve both intents rather than taking one side wholesale
the security suite is the regression gate: it must stay green
verification: symbol probe for the five write methods

legs.goal: Tests, lint, and a per-leg review of the reconciliation. Did anything get lost or silently reverted in the merge?
Drive the reconciled app: entitlement, guest binding, session ownership and admin flows still behave as the security contract requires.
The two backends agree on what counts as a credential, and no input can destroy a stored PAT.
boundaries: the known divergence: _store_credential accepts any non-empty string, so a mask is written to the vault as the credential, while _is_a_real_credential rejects masks. The admin_db_service guard is inert under PostgreSQL because provider_config cannot hold a PAT by constraint
one shared predicate, used by both paths - do not duplicate the rule
verification: table-driven test asserting both paths agree

legs.goal: A newly created agent cannot be born with a masked value as its credential, on either backend.
boundaries: found by the credential-parity runner: routers/admin.py accepts a mask as a valid new cortex_agent_pat on create, so an agent can be created with '********' as its credential. The update path is now guarded; create is not
reuse src/utils/credential_value.is_a_real_credential - do not write a second rule
create must REJECT (a create with no usable credential is an error), unlike update which preserves; state the difference in the commit
mutation-check every assertion

legs.goal: POST /api/v1/agents/register cannot accept a masked value as a credential either.
boundaries: found by create-path-credential-guard: agents.py:134 declares cortex_agent_pat as a plain required str, so a mask is accepted. It populates the in-memory registry, so the effect is an agent that lists fine and fails every Snowflake call
reuse src/utils/credential_value.is_a_real_credential - assert function identity in a test so a future copy-paste fails
reject like create does, do not preserve
mutation-check every assertion

legs.goal: /process routes enforce entitlement to the agent named in the request body, closing a surface the security branch turned from inert to live.
boundaries: CRITICAL, found by code-judge-S1. At merge-base ProcessRequest had no agent_id so chat.py:151 would raise and the endpoint was inert. The security branch added agent_id and router-level get_current_user, making it LIVE and AUTHENTICATED but never entitled
get_current_user accepts guest tokens, so a guest bound to agent alpha can POST /process/ with agent_id beta and spend beta's Cortex PAT
consume src/middleware/entitlements.py rather than writing a second rule
tests/security R9 only covers anonymous and wrong-key on /process; there is no cross-agent test - add one

while here: chat.py:91 and dynamic_chat.py:127 carry loose bool(x.get('isAdmin') or ...) duplicates of the strict predicate. Not currently exploitable because get_current_user normalises to a real bool, but entitlements.is_platform_admin is public and takes an arbitrary claims dict. Consolidate onto is_admin_claim
verification: guest bound to A refused on B via /process

legs.goal: A caller cannot read or append to another user's conversation by passing their session_id to chat.
boundaries: HIGH, found by code-judge-S1. ChatRequest.session_id is caller-supplied and SessionClient.get_session_messages/add_message have no requester scoping, unlike agent_session_service which the guarded read routes use correctly

so a caller entitled to agent A passes another user's session_id to POST /agents/chat, loads their history as model context and appends to it - reading through the front door what GET /{id}/sessions/{sid}/messages correctly refuses
session-service is an external service outside this repo: if ownership cannot be enforced at its boundary, enforce it before the call and say so
mutation-check every assertion
verification: a foreign session_id is refused on /agents/chat
the owner's own session still works

legs.goal: PgAgentRepository and the two mapping repositories are correct and complete: right conflict target, no undeletable rows, and every column the application reads survives a round trip.
boundaries: MERGED from mapping-conflict-target and read-path-columns: both rewrite the same file, so one runner owns it

both mapping callers mint a fresh uuid4 per call, so ON CONFLICT (legacy_id) can NEVER fire - the real conflict is (agent_id, group_id) and (user_id, group_id). copy_wave2 targets legacy_id, correct for a one-shot migration and wrong here
delete_all matches WHERE legacy_id = ANY(%s), so a NULL legacy_id row is permanently undeletable - never write one
a role of 'Agent_Manager' was silently dropped once: normalise case before the enum cast

_select() omits queue_name, tool_choice, max_threads, session_ttl_days, max_session_messages, rate_limit_per_minute, rate_limit_per_hour, tools_enabled, guest_access_enabled. engineering_ai has queue_name='engineering' in dev and would silently fall back to 'default', sending its RQ jobs to the wrong queue

the guest flag WRITE path fails loudly too: _UPDATABLE has no guestAccessEnabled entry while admin_db_service updatable_fields does, so update_fields raises ValueError, and routers/admin.py catches ValueError BEFORE HTTPException - an admin toggling guest access on PG gets HTTP 404 with the internal column allowlist in the body. PgAgentRepository.put also omits it, so creation silently stores false
behaviour judge confirmed the read side fails CLOSED (guest gets 404), so it is a functionality regression not a security hole

YOU ALSO OWN tests/pg/conftest.py: _reachable catches bare Exception, so a missing psycopg driver is misreported as a missing database and PGTEST_REQUIRED then fails with a misleading reason. Cheap to fix while you are in there; not required by any check
verification: PGTEST_REQUIRED=1 pytest tests/pg against a database at alembic head

legs.goal: A caller-supplied thread_id cannot be used to reach another user's thread.
boundaries: found by chat-session-ownership: thread_id is the IDENTICAL defect to session_id - caller-supplied, unscoped, passed to generate_response and written via set_thread_id
that leg established the pattern: verify ownership before the call, refuse 404 to match how the entitlement layer refuses an unseen agent, reuse PLACEHOLDER_OWNER_IDS rather than duplicating it

the same trap applies: both handlers wrap their body in except Exception returning 200 with success:false, which would convert a 404 into a 200 and leave the guard decorative. Re-raise HTTPException first
platform admins keep unscoped reach, as the read and delete routes already grant
mutation-check every assertion; the previous leg had one mutation survive its first battery because no test exercised the placeholder-owner branch
verification: a foreign thread_id is refused on chat
the owner's own thread still works

legs.goal: PgAgentRepository put, update_fields and delete are proven substitutable for the DynamoDB implementation against a real database.
boundaries: mirror the patterns in test_pg_wave1.py
conftest clean() covers only iam tables - extend it to catalog.agent_groups and catalog.agents or tests will leak into each other
bring the database to alembic head, not sql/0001, because guest_access_enabled comes from 0003
legs.note: runner killed by API error after writing tests; coach validated and mutation-checked, then committed

legs.goal: agent-service tests/pg actually execute in CI instead of skipping silently.
boundaries: auth-service has a pg job and PGTEST_REQUIRED; agent-service has neither, so every new wave-2 test would skip and read as green
mirror the existing auth-service job rather than inventing a new shape
tests/pg/conftest.py _reachable catches bare Exception, so a missing psycopg driver is misreported as a missing database - PGTEST_REQUIRED then fails with a misleading reason

testpaths omits tests/db and tests/pg: 7 and 3 files on disk are not collected by a bare pytest. CI is unaffected because it passes tests/ explicitly, but a local developer gets a false green - and tests/pg/test_pg_agent_writes.py plus test_pg_mapping_puts.py are exactly the ACC-MERGE-003 coverage
verification: the job fails when the database is absent and PGTEST_REQUIRED is set
legs.evidence: already satisfied on this branch: job pg-integration-test (.gitlab-ci.yml:194) brings up postgres:16-alpine, runs alembic upgrade head in db-schema (line 229) so the database is at HEAD including 0003, then runs BOTH auth-service and agent-service tests/pg with PGTEST_REQUIRED=1. agent-service conftest.py:94 honours the flag and raises rather than skipping. The earlier research claim that agent-service had no pg job was reading develop, not the reconciled branch.

legs.goal: The credential predicate refuses the mask shapes real admin UIs actually produce, not only the three that were enumerated.
boundaries: found by the S2 behaviour judge and confirmed by the coach. MASK_CHARACTERS is '*BULLET-MIDDOT-CIRCLE-BULLETOP' only, so these all read as REAL credentials today: partial reveal 'dots+abcd' (the one that matters - real admin forms render it and it would overwrite a live PAT), U+2217, U+FF0A fullwidth, U+204E, U+25CB, and a zero-width space which str.strip() does not remove

the partial-reveal case is the hard one: it is a real string with real characters, so a pure character-class rule cannot catch it. Think about what distinguishes a masked value from a credential rather than extending the character list and calling it done
whatever rule you choose must keep every currently-accepted real credential accepted - check the existing parity tests before and after
one shared predicate still: do not add a second rule anywhere
mutation-check every assertion

legs.goal: Tests, lint, types, and a parallel review per leg. Are the new tests mutation-proof, or do they pass against a broken implementation?
Against a real PostgreSQL, drive the write paths as the application does and confirm every WRITE, CRED and PARITY check.
One MR carrying the reconciled wave-2 work, with a real description, a green pipeline, and no protected branch pushed.
boundaries: target develop, never push to it directly
the description must state the rollback data cost, not just the feature
verification: MR state opened with a description

legs.goal: The reconciled branch is merged to develop via MR, which is the ONLY way an image containing revision 0003 can ever be built.
boundaries: HARD PREREQUISITE, established by research: the db-schema image builds ONLY on branch develop or db-PostgreSQL (.gitlab-ci.yml:502-504). feat/wave2-cutover-reconciled builds nothing, so 0003 cannot reach any environment from it
verified: all 26 published db-schema tags were resolved SHA->tree and NONE contains 0003
merge through the MR, never push to develop directly
REQUIRES EXPLICIT OWNER APPROVAL before merging - this lands the wave-2 work AND the 10-commit security branch on develop together
record the resulting image tag: the format is <prefix>-<pipeline_iid>.<short_sha> and the sha identifies the exact build commit
verification: a db-schema image tag exists whose sha contains 0003

legs.goal: dev's db-migrate image pin points at a build containing 0003, and the PostSync hook has applied it.
boundaries: dev only - never apps/stage or apps/prod
this pin is NEVER auto-bumped: the gitops auto-bump job rewrites only agent-service, auth-service and registry-service. Every db-migrate bump in history is a hand-written commit
migrations run as an ArgoCD PostSync hook Job (helm/db-migrate/templates/job.yaml:12,54) executing `alembic upgrade head` from the pinned image, with ALEMBIC_VERSION_TABLE_SCHEMA=ops
ArgoCD excludes hook manifests from its diff, so an image-tag-only change may not reliably drive OutOfSync. After committing, explicitly run `argocd app sync aihub-dev-db-migrate` rather than waiting
do NOT apply the DDL by hand with the migrator credential: the immutable-tag policy exists so nothing changes what the Job applies without a gitops change
legs.baseline: dev PG pre-0003 baseline: alembic=0002_pat_alias_case, guest_access_enabled_col=0, agents=7, user_groups=49, agent_groups=19, pat_secret_arn=5/7
legs.note: pin lives in apps/dev/db-migrate/values.yaml, isolated from update_gitops_develop sed
legs.evidence: gitops !77 merged (main bb31cdf88b). ArgoCD reported Synced/Healthy WITHOUT running the hook - all chart resources are helm hooks, excluded from sync comparison. Required an explicit sync operation. Job db-migrate Complete 1/1; log shows "Running upgrade 0002_pat_alias_case -> 0003_agent_guest_access".

legs.goal: A dev image containing the resolver and all five write methods is running, with DB_BACKEND_WAVE2 still absent.
boundaries: prove the image with the symbol probe, never by comparing tags
the flag stays absent in this leg - this is wave 1's lesson, prove the image separately from the flag

ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: read-path-columns makes the application SELECT guest_access_enabled. db-migrate and agent-service are SEPARATE ArgoCD Applications with no ordering between them and a failed migration does not stop the app rolling out, so the migration must be confirmed applied BEFORE this image deploys or the app queries a column that does not exist
verification: symbol probe prints True three times
pod Running, DB_BACKEND_WAVE2 absent from env
legs.note: db-schema Dockerfile ships only alembic.ini/checks.py/migrations/sql, ENTRYPOINT alembic, boto3 absent from requirements.txt. PostSync hook applies DDL ONLY. Copy re-run is out-of-band from a workstation with psycopg+boto3.
legs.evidence: dev PG: alembic=0003_agent_guest_access, guest_access_enabled column present, agents=7, pat_secret_arn=5/7 unchanged. agent-service+auth-service running dev-676.0cb30b5f.

legs.goal: dev data agrees between the two stores on every column the application reads.
boundaries: the verify checksum compares only slug, name, provider, is_active - it must cover the columns in ACC-PARITY-001 or a wrongly copied value passes silently
re-run the copy after 0003 so guest_access_enabled is populated rather than defaulted
cmd_verify checksums source against target over ONE shared `fields` tuple: adding a column means changing it in two places, or verify fails on every row with a bare 'checksum mismatch'
verification: copy_wave2.py verify exits 0 with the widened checksum
legs.note: Run `copy_wave2.py agents` (NOT all). Never --prune: with 7 agents the orphan allowance is max(1,0)=1, so exactly one agent could be deleted silently, cascading to agent_groups/chat. Never --write-secrets: on ResourceExistsException it put_secret_value()s the stale DynamoDB PAT over the live secret. Without it COALESCE preserves all 5 ARNs. Column value alone cannot distinguish copied-false from defaulted-false: prove via updated_at>=copy_start AND xmin change on all 7, plus DynamoDB source id set.
legs.evidence: PARITY PASS 7/7 on the cmd_verify checksum fields (slug,name,provider,is_active,guest_access_enabled), computed independently of copy_wave2.py from a direct DynamoDB scan vs catalog.agents.
legs.decision: Mutating copy re-run DELIBERATELY SKIPPED. All 7 DynamoDB items lack the guestAccessEnabled attribute entirely (0 true, 0 non-bool). Mapper is `guest_access_enabled = raw_guest_access is True`, so the copied value for every row is false - identical to the 0003 column default. The re-run therefore cannot change the target column, while it WOULD overwrite all 17 agent columns from DynamoDB. Risk without benefit; parity proven read-only instead.

legs.goal: Review the MR as a reviewer who has not seen it written. Is the rollback cost stated honestly? Is anything claimed that is not proven?
legs.evidence: C1,C2,C4 VERIFIED against a real PostgreSQL 16 (443 passed tests/pg). C3 REFUTED both directions. C5 MIXED: 4 of 5 mutations killed, 1 survived. ruff/black/isort clean. Baseline held at 5 failed / 1626 passed.
legs.findings: F1 CRITICAL interior-mask accepted as credential, destroys stored PAT, demonstrated end-to-end. F2 CRITICAL _owner_scoped_filter has zero coverage, mutation to unconditional raise survived. F3 HIGH PG outage renders as 404 not 5xx. F4 MEDIUM get_group_by_name fails open, lets create_group overwrite. F5 LOW real secret with >=50pc asterisks rejected. F7 teams-channel write into catalog.agents now contends for agents_slug_key.

legs.goal: Independently confirm the image, the migration and the data parity against live dev, read-only.
legs.evidence: B1-B6 all VERIFIED. B7 found a CRITICAL breaker no row-parity gate could catch: agentType case round-trip is not identity on the PG backend. pg_repositories.py:404 lowercases agentType into storage provider on write; :248 returns row["provider"] straight back as agentType on read. dynamic_chat_service.py:290 compares `agent_type != "Snowflake"` exact-match, and admin.py:58 pins pattern ^(Snowflake|SAP|AWS|Custom)$. Proven live by running both repositories side by side inside the pod: DDB=Snowflake PG=snowflake for all 7 agents. Post-flip every chat returns None and every admin agent PUT 422s, while /health stays green and all 5 gates stay green.

legs.goal: A written revert procedure naming the exact change and every category of write it strands.
boundaries: no .md in the code repo - use a GitLab issue or the MR description
must name the rotated-PAT asymmetry: after a revert the agent uses the old PAT and Cortex 401s with no visible config change
verification: the issue or MR section exists and covers every endpoint in the research table
legs.evidence: Written into gitops !78 description before the flip, per contract. Revert e3fb136 -> ArgoCD auto-syncs; absent DB_BACKEND_WAVE2 means DynamoDB. Includes the three capture queries that must run BEFORE reverting, because rollback is clean for reads and lossy for writes: DynamoDB is never written post-flip, so admin changes made during the PostgreSQL window exist only in PG and a revert strands them.

legs.note: Root cause: repository storage<->domain translation is asymmetric. Fix the round trip in one place, not the consumers.
legs.evidence: branch fix/agenttype-case-roundtrip. New src/db/agent_provider.py is the single source of truth: CANONICAL_AGENT_TYPES + canonical_agent_type() + agent_type_pattern(). _to_item maps the stored slug back to canonical; admin.py derives its pydantic pattern from agent_type_pattern() instead of a duplicated regex, so it cannot drift again. Independently verified by me: round trip identity for all 4 canonical types, unknown slug passes through unmangled, suite 5 failed / 1649 passed (baseline 1626, +23). Mutation: reverting pg_repositories.py failed 18 of 23 new tests.
legs.followUp: pg_repositories.py:533 update_fields lowercases agentType without the slug-shape validation put() has. Pre-existing asymmetry between the two write sites, deliberately left out of scope.

legs.note: F1. Verified independently: abcd****wxyz -> True (overwrites real PAT), s*e*c*r* -> False (rejects valid credential). Majority rule only catches masks whose glyphs are >=50pc.
legs.evidence: branch fix/interior-mask-credential-predicate. Mask detected by run shape, not majority count. Two deliberately separate thresholds both at 3: decorative filler glyphs vs structural credential punctuation (-_.:/+=~ legitimately repeats as base64 == padding). Independently verified by me: 28/28 correct across 16 mask shapes and 12 real credentials, both directions. First round regressed 3 valid credentials (my!!secret, pw##123, a$$b) at threshold 2; caught in review and returned to the runner. Suite 5 failed / 1666 passed. Mutation to the old majority rule: 28 failed.

legs.note: F2. Verified independently: no test file imports agent_session_service. Guard at agent_session_service.py:45 called from :154,:357,:429 backing 3 REST endpoints, entirely unexercised.
legs.evidence: branch test/session-ownership-guard-coverage. 37 tests, no src changes (git diff --stat -- src empty). I re-ran mutation M-A myself: replacing the guard body with an unconditional raise now gives 24 failed / 13 passed, where before it left the suite byte-identical to baseline. Also pins the IMPOSSIBLE_OWNER_PREDICATE branch via a placeholder requester that would self-match under a naive {user_id: requester_id}. Suite 5 failed / 1663 passed.
legs.followUp: requester_id=None bypasses scoping entirely; safe only because AgentAccess.requester_id returns None solely for platform admins. Coupling is implicit and untested at the boundary; behaviour is now pinned by test but the source contract is unchanged.

legs.note: Pinned to the integration branch head. Re-judge after the three fixes; must confirm the original findings are dead and no new ones opened.
Must run against a DEPLOYED image containing the three fixes. Cannot start until !161 merges and the build publishes.

Reviewer BLOCK A/B + CI. put() silently rewrites an unrecognised agentType to snowflake; update_fields() does not, so the two write paths disagree. Six literal definitions of the canonical set survive. tests/pg test_pg_agent_writes.py:671 and :1091 assert the OLD lowercase contract and now fail in CI.

Reviewer BLOCK C. Verified by me: PEM headers, my---secret, pass...word, host=db;pwd=x///y all FALSE-REJECTED; xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-1234, XXXXXXXXXXXX3f9a, abcd**wxyz, ab*cd*ef*gh all wrongly accepted. The 2->3 threshold change I recommended reopened 2-run masks. Root issue: string shape cannot separate a mask from a credential; failure must be loud instead.

legs.goal: DB_BACKEND_WAVE2 is postgres in dev for both services, and every wave-2 repository binds to PostgreSQL.

both files in ONE commit: iam.user_groups is shared and splitting them puts it in two stores
dev ArgoCD is fully automated, so a merge auto-deploys - there is no manual gate

verification: in-pod probe prints Pg* for all four repositories across both services
legs.note: ORDERING CONSTRAINT: copy re-run overwrites all 17 agent columns from DynamoDB unconditionally. It must run BEFORE this flip, while DynamoDB is still authoritative. Re-running it after cutover reverts every Postgres-side admin edit.
legs.evidence: gitops !78 open and deliberately NOT merged. Held by behaviour-judge-S3 finding 1 (CRITICAL) and 2 (HIGH).

legs.goal: The cutover is proven end to end: credentials resolve, chat works, administration works, login is unaffected, and the two broken agents are no worse.
boundaries: use a disposable agent for the create/delete checks, never a real one
do not mint credentials for the two PAT-less agents - prove only that they are unchanged

CANARY: Facilities F&Q (agent-4426745d) is the designated first agent, chosen on evidence not convenience. Parity proven before cutover: identity, host, database DEV_TDEV_ANALYTICS_DB, schema FAQSCHATBOOT, cortex name FACILITIES_FAQ and warehouse all match; PAT correctly absent from provider_config with has_pat_arn=True and alias agent-4426745d; and every column the read path drops is unset in BOTH stores for this agent, so the known read-path gap cannot affect it. Verify it first: first chat, first admin edit. If it misbehaves, revert rather than continue

engineering_ai is the opposite case - it has queue_name='engineering' and WILL silently fall back to 'default' until read-path-columns lands, sending its RQ jobs to the wrong queue. Do not use it as the canary

KNOWN BEHAVIOUR CHANGE AT CUTOVER: create_teams_channel (admin_db_service.py ~705) assigns the teams table then never uses it, writes the channel into catalog.agents via agent_repository.put, and returns a read of the teams table the write never reached. Broken today; under PostgreSQL the item has no agentType so agents_provider_ck rejects it and the endpoint 500s instead of failing silently. Verify whether Teams surface is exercised at all before treating a 500 there as a cutover regression
verification: admin create, update and delete each visible in catalog.agents
the internal by-entra lookup returning groups and roles

revert, prove every wave-2 repository binds back to DynamoDB and the service is healthy, then re-apply the cutover

use only the disposable agent from cutover-verify - this deliberately strands whatever was written to PostgreSQL in between, which is the behaviour being demonstrated, so nothing real may be in flight
keep admin traffic off for both rolls
verification: in-pod probe shows DynamoDB classes after the revert and Pg* again after re-applying
